source_refs.note: Exercise 10.2 Q10 (i)-(ii), book p.190 (PDF 195). Key PDF 308: (i) 33/65, -56/65 matches; (ii) 416/425, 3/5 wrong (correct -304/425, 297/425). Sympy; solution book PDF 919-922 agrees.

blocks.prompt: 10 (i) Find \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\) and \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\), given that \(\tan\alpha = \dfrac{3}{4}\), \(\cos\beta = \dfrac{5}{13}\) and neither the terminal side of the angle of measure \(\alpha\) nor that of \(\beta\) is in the quadrant I.
blocks.explanation:
Yahan quadrants seedhe nahi bataye gaye; signs aur shart "quadrant I mein nahi" se khud nikalne hain. Yeh sawal do kaam jodta hai: pehle quadrant ki pehchaan, phir sum ke formulas.
Phir chaaron ratios nikal kar sum ke formulas lagane hain.
Plan: \(\alpha\) ka quadrant, \(\beta\) ka quadrant, missing ratios, formulas.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}\), \(\cos\beta = \frac{5}{13}\); koi angle quadrant I mein nahi.
Humein find karna hai: \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\) aur \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\).
Tareeqa: pehle quadrants, phir \(\sin\alpha, \cos\alpha, \sin\beta\) sahi signs ke saath, phir:
\[\sin(\alpha + \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta + \cos\alpha\sin\beta\]
\[\cos(\alpha + \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta\]

Quadrants tay karein
\[\tan\alpha > 0 \Rightarrow \text{I or III} \Rightarrow \alpha \in \text{III}\]
\[\cos\beta > 0 \Rightarrow \text{I or IV} \Rightarrow \beta \in \text{IV}\]
Kyun: Tangent quadrant I aur III mein positive hota hai, cosine I aur IV mein. Sawal ne quadrant I mana kar diya hai, is liye har angle ke liye ek hi option bachta hai.
Dhyan dein: Shart \"neither ... in quadrant I\" ko nazar andaz kar ke sab kuch positive le lena sab se aam ghalti hai.

\(\alpha\) ke ratios (quadrant III)
\[\sec^2\alpha = 1 + \dfrac{9}{16} = \dfrac{25}{16}\]
\[\cos\alpha = -\dfrac{4}{5},\quad \sin\alpha = \tan\alpha\cos\alpha = -\dfrac{3}{5}\]
Kyun: \(1 + \tan^2\alpha = \sec^2\alpha\) se \(\sec\alpha = \pm\frac{5}{4}\). Quadrant III mein cosine negative, to \(\cos\alpha = -\frac{4}{5}\). Phir \(\sin\alpha = \tan\alpha \times \cos\alpha = \frac{3}{4} \times (-\frac{4}{5})\), jo negative hai, aur quadrant III mein sine waqai negative hota hai.

\(\beta\) ka ratio (quadrant IV)
\[\sin\beta = -\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{25}{169}} = -\dfrac{12}{13}\]
Kyun: \(169 - 25 = 144\), \(\sqrt{144} = 12\). Quadrant IV mein sine negative hota hai.

\(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\) nikalein
\[= \left(-\dfrac{3}{5}\right)\dfrac{5}{13} + \left(-\dfrac{4}{5}\right)\left(-\dfrac{12}{13}\right)\]
\[= -\dfrac{15}{65} + \dfrac{48}{65} = \dfrac{33}{65}\]
Kyun: Pehla product negative, doosra (do negatives) positive. Denominator \(5 \times 13 = 65\).

\(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\) nikalein
\[= \left(-\dfrac{4}{5}\right)\dfrac{5}{13} - \left(-\dfrac{3}{5}\right)\left(-\dfrac{12}{13}\right)\]
\[= -\dfrac{20}{65} - \dfrac{36}{65} = -\dfrac{56}{65}\]
Kyun: Doosra product \(+\frac{36}{65}\) hai, lekin formula ka minus usay ghata deta hai.

Tasdeeq
\[33^2 + 56^2 = 1089 + 3136 = 4225 = 65^2 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Ek hi angle \(\alpha + \beta\) ke sine aur cosine hain, to squares ka jama 1 hona chahiye, aur hai. Answer key bhi \(\frac{33}{65}, -\frac{56}{65}\) deta hai.

blocks.prompt: 10 (ii) Find \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\) and \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\), given that \(\tan\alpha = -\dfrac{15}{8}\) and \(\sin\beta = -\dfrac{7}{25}\) and neither the terminal side of the angle of measure \(\alpha\) nor that of \(\beta\) is in the quadrant IV.
blocks.explanation:
Phir se quadrants khud nikalne hain, is dafa shart hai "quadrant IV mein nahi".
Tareeqa bilkul part (i) wala hai; farq sirf signs aur shart ka hai, is liye har sign soch samajh kar lagayen.
Plan: quadrants, missing ratios, formulas, aur aakhir mein \(\sin^2 + \cos^2 = 1\) se tasdeeq.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\tan\alpha = -\frac{15}{8}\), \(\sin\beta = -\frac{7}{25}\); koi angle quadrant IV mein nahi.
Humein find karna hai: \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\) aur \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\).
Tareeqa: quadrants, phir \(\sin\alpha, \cos\alpha, \cos\beta\), phir sum ke formulas (part (i) wale).

Quadrants tay karein
\[\tan\alpha < 0 \Rightarrow \text{II or IV} \Rightarrow \alpha \in \text{II}\]
\[\sin\beta < 0 \Rightarrow \text{III or IV} \Rightarrow \beta \in \text{III}\]
Kyun: Tangent negative sirf II aur IV mein; sine negative sirf III aur IV mein. Quadrant IV mana hai, to \(\alpha\) II mein aur \(\beta\) III mein.

\(\alpha\) ke ratios (quadrant II)
\[\sec^2\alpha = 1 + \dfrac{225}{64} = \dfrac{289}{64}\]
\[\cos\alpha = -\dfrac{8}{17},\quad \sin\alpha = \tan\alpha\cos\alpha = \dfrac{15}{17}\]
Kyun: \(64 + 225 = 289 = 17^2\). Quadrant II mein cosine negative; \(\sin\alpha = (-\frac{15}{8})(-\frac{8}{17}) = \frac{15}{17}\), positive, jaisa quadrant II mein hona chahiye.

\(\beta\) ka ratio (quadrant III)
\[\cos\beta = -\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{49}{625}} = -\dfrac{24}{25}\]
Kyun: \(625 - 49 = 576 = 24^2\). Quadrant III mein cosine negative.

\(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\) nikalein
\[= \left(-\dfrac{8}{17}\right)\left(-\dfrac{24}{25}\right) - \dfrac{15}{17}\left(-\dfrac{7}{25}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{192}{425} + \dfrac{105}{425} = \dfrac{297}{425}\]
Kyun: Pehla product positive \(\frac{192}{425}\); doosra \(-\frac{105}{425}\), aur us se pehle minus, to plus ho gaya.

Tasdeeq
\[304^2 + 297^2 = 92416 + 88209\]
\[= 180625 = 425^2 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(\sin^2 + \cos^2 = 1\) poora ho gaya, yani dono jawab aapas mein durust hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Part (ii) ke liye answer key \(\frac{416}{425}\) aur \(\frac{3}{5}\) deta hai. Yeh ek hi angle ke sine aur cosine ho hi nahi sakte, kyunke \(\left(\frac{416}{425}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^2 \ne 1\), aur yeh kitab ke data se bhi nahi nikalte. Sahi jawab \(\sin(\alpha + \beta) = -\frac{304}{425}\), \(\cos(\alpha + \beta) = \frac{297}{425}\) hai.
